thread.title: Tech Data CEO’s game plan for rapid growth involves knocking on a lot of doors

author: Margie Manning
title: Tech Data CEO’s game plan for rapid growth involves knocking on a lot of doors
text: – Finance Editor, Tampa Bay   2:49pm EST When Bob Dutkowsky joined Tech Data Corp. as CEO in 2006, the company had just over $20 billion in annual revenue. On Thursday, the Clearwater-based IT distributor said it posted more than 50 percent of that annual amount in a single quarter, recording $11.1 billion in sales for the three months ended Jan. 31. Tech Data (NASDAQ: TECD), now the largest company in Florida with $36.8 billion in sales for fiscal year 2018 , is also the first technology firm to top the list of Florida companies, a benchmark for a state whose economy has long been dominated by the tourism and retailing sectors. “Florida’s economy has become remarkably more diverse over the past few decades and is now home to a large and growing technology and aerospace sector,” Wells Fargo Securities wrote in an October 2017 report. Tech Data's move into the No. 1 spot "truly defines us as a tech hub,” said Jill St. Thomas , co-executive director of Tampa Bay Tech, Florida’s largest technology council. “As the second-fastest growing tech hub in the nation, we are thrilled to see Tech Data amplifying the tech story of Tampa Bay. Tech Data’s exceptional growth, combined with their unwavering commitment to this community, is a win for everyone." Dutkowsky echoed those sentiments in an interview with the Tampa Bay Business Journal . “It helps to have a company that’s a pacesetter,” he said. “A company like ours can help make a community a better place to live and learn and work.” Tech Data employs about 14,000 people worldwide, including about 2,000 workers locally, so it doesn’t have the jobs impact of business such as Publix Super Markets Inc. with 193,000 workers and the former No. 1 company in Florida. Tech Data’s business model is different, Dutkowsky said, and the company is more efficient. “We don’t have storefronts or brick and mortar. Our business comes to us digitally, with customer orders over the web,” he said. Tech Data’s financial gains in fiscal 2018 came largely from the $2.6 billion acquisition of the technology solutions business of Avnet Inc. (NYSE: AVT) in February 2017. That deal gave Tech Data a presence in a new market, the Asia-Pacific region, as well as an expanded portfolio of products and services. “We’re calling on more customers in more places. We’re now in 100 countries and we have more sales capabilities in those countries,” Dutkowsky said. “The combination of a broad set of products and services with more aggressive outreach is the reason we’re growing.” Sales in the just-ended fourth quarter were led by networking products, personal computers and mobility products, including Apple Inc .’s (NASDAQ: AAPL) iPhone 10 that started to ship in the fall. Apple represented 19 percent of Tech Data’s worldwide sales in the fourth quarter, Dutkowsky told analysts on a conference call. Small and medium-size business initiatives performed well, growing by double digits in Q4, Dutkowsky said on the conference call. Tech Data is covering the SMB sector aggressively, he told TBBJ . “It’s easy to find Fortune 100 companies, but there are literally tens of thousands of small businesses that need to compete against those big guys, but no one knows where they are unless you go out and find them,” Dutkowsky said. “Technology makes the little companies look bigger, and the big companies use technology to make their workforce more productive.” With its global operations, Tech Data will see a mixed impact from the new federal tax law, Dutkowsky said. The U.S. tax rate will fall, but there’s also a provision that will allow the government to tax the company’s foreign profits, he said. “In the long run, our tax rate will be lower, but in the short term it’s not a big advantage to a company like Tech Data,” Dutkowsky said. The company is considering repatriating some of its overseas cash, but has not made a decision on that, he said. Although Tech Data’s annual income jumped 40 percent, its net income, including one-time charges such as acquisition-related expenses, fell to $116.6 million for fiscal 2018, a 40 percent decline. The company’s stock fell more than 18 percent and was trading at $87.90 at midday. – Finance Editor, Tampa Bay   2:49pm EST Related Content
